summary: 1934 Aermotor fire tower in Sawyer County, unused for about five years by 2015; a 1991 state record says the fire tower was moved from Connors Lake to the area headquarters in 1973.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with US Forest Service-style stairway (register); Park Falls Ranger Station tower cabin built during the CCC program (1991 state record)
facts.status_note: Registry lists it standing. A 2015 report said it had not been used in five years, and the state planned to retire it in 2016. No later visit or removal record found.

staffing.status: not used for about five years

events.note: Register gives May 1934 as the build date.

The 1991 state record gives 1935 as the construction date of the Park Falls Ranger Station tower cabin (its header says 1936). A September 1936 CCC newsletter still described a tower cabin at Connors Lake as planned, with lumber on hand, so the 1935 date may not belong to the Connors Lake cabin.
CCC camp newsletter says the tower aided fire crews and a tower cabin was to be built.

The 1991 state record says the fire tower was moved from its original site at Connor Lake to the area headquarters, January to July 1973, when it was not used. The record is about the cabin, so it is unclear whether the tower itself or only the cabin moved.
Statewide retirement decision; the Connors Lake tower had not been used for about five years.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1991 record gives 1935 as the construction date of the Park Falls Ranger Station tower cabin, and its header says 1936. A September 1936 CCC newsletter still described a Connors Lake tower cabin as planned, with lumber on hand. The two may be different cabins, so the Connors Lake cabin build date is unresolved.
The state record spells it Connor Lake; the register and the registry spell it Connors Lake. The story uses Connors Lake.

sources.title: DNR will discontinue fire towers in 2016

notes_for_editor: The 1991 record is about the Park Falls Ranger Station tower cabin and says 'the fire tower was moved' from Connor Lake in 1973. It is unclear whether the steel tower or only the cabin left the site; if the tower left, the registry's standing entry at the lake is probably stale. The 2015 article's year is inferred: the printed page has no date, but it cites a Dec. 16 DNR release and 2016 retirement. Current condition and access are unknown. The lake is spelled two ways across sources.
